Article Title: Consistent Infosystems launches Con Data Locker External HDD in 1TB and 2TB storage options; price starts at Rs 18,999
Article Text: Consistent Infosystems has launched Con Data Locker Ex. HDD 1TB (CTH2CSCA) and Con Data Locker Ex. HDD 2TB (CTH2DSCA). The external hard drives combine a compact form factor with a sleek, modern design and are suited for everyday use across home, office and professional environments. The new External HDD range provides ample space for storing photos, videos, music, documents, games and backup files, making it suitable for both personal and professional use. Featuring a sleek black finish with a textured, ribbed surface, the drives have a modern and compact design that makes them easy to carry between home, office and while travelling.The Con Data Locker Ex. HDD 1TB and 2TB come with Type-C connectivity and support up to 450 MB/s reading speeds and transfer rates of up to 6 Gbps, enabling convenient movement of data and files.Compatible with Windows, Mac OS and Linux, both external HDD variants offer flexibility across different devices and operating systems. The devices are built with durable ABS construction, the drives are suitable for regular storage and backup requirements, while their compact and portable form factor makes them convenient to carry and use.For added convenience, the drives offer a Plug & Play experience and reliable performance, enabling users to connect and access their data without complex setup. Yogesh Agrawal , CMD and Co-Founder, Consistent Infosystems, said, “As the volume of digital content continues to grow, users increasingly require convenient and reliable ways to store, transfer and back up their data. Our new External HDD range is designed to address these everyday storage requirements with flexible capacity options, portability and ease of use. With the 1TB and 2TB variants, we aim to provide practical storage solutions for both personal and professional users. ”The Consistent Con Data Locker Ex. HDD range is available in 1TB and 2TB storage capacities. The 1TB variant carries an MRP of Rs 18,999, while the 2TB variant carries an MRP of Rs 34,999. The products are available through shop.consistent.in and other leading retail channels.
Article Summary: Consistent Infosystems has launched Con Data Locker Ex. HDD 1TB and 2TB. The external hard drives combine a compact form factor with a sleek, modern design. The products are available through shop.consistent.in and other leading retail channels.

Article Title: Sam Altman-backed Praxis plans $1 billion AI-powered town in Uruguay; first residents expected in mid-2027 with homes, resorts and cultural spaces for the AI era
Article Text:
An aerial concept rendering of Praxis’s proposed waterfront resort in Uruguay, featuring minimalist architecture, a swimming pool and landscaped surroundings. (Image: Praxis)

Sam Altman-backed Praxis selects Uruguay for its $1 billion AI-powered town

$1 billion investment planned over several years

First residents expected in mid-2027

Homes, resorts and cultural spaces planned

A community designed around the AI era

Sam Altman's connection to Praxis

+Colonia provides the physical foundation

Who is expected to live there?

The project remains in its early stages

Praxis, a technology-focused community backed by Apollo Projects, a fund associated with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, has selected Uruguay for its first physical development. The project involves a projected investment of about $1 billion in the +Colonia development near Colonia del Sacramento. The first Praxis residents are expected to arrive around mid-2027, while construction of the larger community continues over the following years. Plans include private residences, a resort and spaces for art, music and other cultural activities. Praxis presents the project as an experiment in how communities could live and organise in a future shaped by artificial intelligence.After searching for a location for about two years, Praxis chose +Colonia, a waterfront urban development near Colonia del Sacramento, as the home of its first physical community. The location offers access to the Río de la Plata and is close to both Montevideo and Buenos Aires. Eduardo Bastitta, founder of +Colonia, has described the partnership as an opportunity to bring together technology, entrepreneurship and new forms of community living.Praxis says its wider online community has more than 150,000 members, including entrepreneurs, investors and people working in technology and artificial intelligence.About 2,700 members have expressed interest in moving to or investing in the Uruguay project. Rather than creating a completely new city on undeveloped land, Praxis is establishing its community within the existing +Colonia development, where construction is already underway.The $1 billion figure attached to the project represents projected investment, rather than money already spent on construction. According to El País and El Observador, the initial Praxis area is expected to cover approximately 350,000 square metres, or roughly 20% of the planned +Colonia urbanisation.Much of the projected spending is expected to be connected to residences and other facilities that Praxis members will purchase or develop. The land transaction is also expected to progress in stages. El País reported that the land sale had not been completed when Praxis announced the project, meaning the full development remains dependent on subsequent agreements, purchases and construction.The first members of the Praxis community are expected to arrive at +Colonia around mid-2027, but that date does not represent the completion of the wider project.Instead, early residents are expected to move into buildings already being developed at +Colonia while the dedicated Praxis neighbourhood takes shape. This allows the community to establish a physical presence before the full range of planned facilities is completed.Dryden Brown, Praxis's co-founder and CEO, is also expected to relocate to Uruguay as the project gets underway.The proposed community is designed to combine residential life with hospitality and cultural activities. Praxis plans private residences, a resort and spaces for art and music, alongside studios, galleries and workshops.The company's vision also includes restaurants, nightlife venues, gardens, public squares, a waterfront promenade and a beach club. Photography, film and music production spaces are also planned, while fellowship programmes could bring artists, musicians, designers, writers and founders to the community.Concept images released by Praxis show minimalist buildings with large glass openings, landscaped areas and pools overlooking the waterfront. These remain proposed designs and do not guarantee that every structure shown will ultimately be built in the same form.The physical development is closely tied to Praxis's broader philosophy about the impact of artificial intelligence. The organisation says it wants to develop new cultural, economic and governance systems for what it describes as a post-AGI world.Its vision is centred on bringing together people involved in technology, entrepreneurship and creative fields and giving them a physical environment in which to live and collaborate as AI changes work and economic activity.However, the currently announced plans do not establish that the town will have AI-controlled utilities, autonomous transport or an AI-run government. The confirmed physical plans focus on housing, hospitality, cultural facilities and community spaces. In this context, the description of the project as “AI-powered” primarily reflects Praxis's technology-driven vision rather than a confirmed specification for all of its infrastructure.Altman's connection to the project comes through Apollo Projects, which Uruguayan media identify as a fund associated with the OpenAI CEO and one of Praxis's backers.That connection does not mean Altman personally owns or is directly developing the Uruguay project, nor does it mean OpenAI is building the community. Praxis is led by Brown, who has described the development as a way to explore how people might live, work and find purpose as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly influential.The involvement of an Altman-associated fund nevertheless places the project within the wider network of technology and AI investment that has emerged around the development of new communities and infrastructure.Praxis is entering a development that already exists rather than starting with an empty site. +Colonia is being built as a large waterfront community near Colonia del Sacramento, with construction already underway.The existing buildings provide a starting point for Praxis's first residents, while the dedicated neighbourhood can be developed progressively. According to El Observador, the initial Praxis area would account for roughly one-fifth of the broader +Colonia urbanisation.This arrangement also explains why the first residents can arrive in 2027 even though the larger project is expected to take considerably longer to develop.Praxis's wider community includes more than 150,000 people, but only a small portion are currently expected to relocate to Uruguay. Around 2,700 members have indicated interest in moving to or investing in the project.The proposed community is aimed at a mix of entrepreneurs, investors, technology professionals and creative workers. Alongside residential facilities, the planned studios, galleries, restaurants and cultural spaces are intended to encourage interaction between those groups.The result is intended to be less a conventional residential development and more a concentrated community built around technology, business and creative activity.Despite its ambitious scale and futuristic designs, the Praxis development remains an evolving project. The $1 billion figure is a projection for future investment, while land acquisition and construction are expected to proceed in stages.For now, the most immediate milestone is the planned arrival of the first Praxis residents around mid-2027. The larger neighbourhood, including its homes, resort and cultural facilities, is expected to take shape over the years that follow.If the plans proceed as announced, the Uruguay project will give Praxis its first permanent physical base and turn its vision of an AI-era community from an online experiment into a real-world development.
Article Summary: Praxis, a technology-focused community, has selected Uruguay for its first physical development. The project involves a projected investment of about $1 billion in the +Colonia development near Colonia del Sacramento. The first Praxis residents are expected to arrive around mid-2027. Plans include private residences, a resort and spaces for art, music and other cultural activities.

Article Title: McDonald's says its AI-enabled drive-thru system can now take orders in English and Spanish with 90% accuracy; it could save at least 50 labour hours a week; CFO Ian Borden notes that company has no i
Article Text:
$8.5 billion global modernization plan of McDonald’s

Archy and ArchIQ: AI at the center of the plan

Beyond AI: physical store upgrades

Menu changes driven by protein demand

Staying focused on value amid cost-of-living pressure

Employee training and customer value

McDonald’s announced that its AI-enabled drive-thru system called Archy can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy. According to a report by CBS, the company said that the system could save at least 50 labour hours per week at a typical restaurant by streamlining order-taking. CFO Ian Borden also stressed that the intention is not to reduce staff but to free employees to focus on hospitality and food preparation tasks, such as hand-breading chicken.The announcement came as McDonald’s unveiled a $8.5 billion investment plan over the next decade to modernize its 46,000 restaurants worldwide. CEO Chris Kempczinski said the company must improve productivity and capture market share in a flat fast-food traffic environment. Planned upgrades include lockers for delivery orders, redesigned kitchen layouts, bigger play areas, and more visible coffee preparation stations to enhance quality perceptions.A key piece of the modernization push is McDonald's AI-enabled drive-thru ordering system, Archy, which the company says can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy. According to CFO Ian Borden, the system could eventually save at least 50 labor hours per week at a typical restaurant.Importantly, Borden was clear that the goal isn't to cut staffing — instead, employees freed up from order-taking would be redirected toward hospitality-focused tasks or hands-on food preparation work, like hand-breading chicken.Archy operates alongside ArchIQ, a broader AI system McDonald's developed in partnership with Google that's designed to improve order accuracy while automating backend tasks like inventory management and staff scheduling. Kempczinski said early testing shows customers have responded well to Archy specifically because it makes their orders more accurate, adding that the company's approach to AI isn't rooted in treating the technology as inherently good or bad, but in being deliberate about how it's actually deployed.The modernization plan extends well past software. McDonald's said upcoming restaurant redesigns will include lockers for handling delivery orders, more visible coffee preparation areas meant to improve customers' perception of quality, larger play areas, and reworked kitchen layouts. Order-accuracy scales, already active in 10,000 restaurants globally, are set to expand to 20,000 locations by 2028.On the food side, McDonald's highlighted strong results from its hand-breaded chicken, currently rolled out across 10,000 restaurants in Asia and a small number of locations near Chicago, with plans to expand testing into additional US markets and Ireland next year — a category where rivals like Chick-fil-A and KFC have long had an edge. The company also plans to introduce grilled chicken sandwiches and wraps, along with experimenting with items like egg bites and bowls.Skye Anderson, president of McDonald's USA, tied this shift directly to changing consumer habits, noting that roughly 30 million Americans currently use GLP-1 weight loss drugs and are increasingly seeking smaller, protein-dense meals as a result. She pointed to internal research suggesting a much larger opportunity, though, with roughly 60 million Americans actively looking to add more protein to their diets overall — a gap she framed as a chance for McDonald's to give customers more reasons to choose the brand first.Despite the modernization push, Kempczinski emphasized that value remains central to McDonald's strategy, particularly for lower-income consumers. He defined low-income US households as those earning $45,000 or less annually, noting that while this group still eats fast food, they're doing so less frequently than before. He credited meal bundles like the $5 meal deal with helping address that pressure, and said McDonald's is exploring introducing entry-level pricing on a basic menu of items in the US, mirroring an approach it already uses in Europe and other markets. He described the current economic backdrop as one demanding constant attention to value, noting that cost-of-living pressure on consumers isn't going away anytime soon.McDonald’s is also rolling out new hospitality-focused training, showing employees what a perfectly cooked Big Mac tastes like and encouraging more pleasant customer interactions. At the same time, the company remains focused on value, exploring entry-level pricing for basic menu items in the U.S. to counter cost-of-living pressures.
Article Summary: McDonald’s announced that its AI-enabled drive-thru system called Archy can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy. The company said that the system could save at least 50 labour hours per week at a typical restaurant by streamlining order-taking. CFO Ian Borden stressed that the intention is not to reduce staff but to free employees to focus on hospitality and food preparation tasks, such as hand-breading chicken.

Article Title: In 2023, Jeff Bezos’ Earth Fund pledged $100 million for Pacific conservation; three years later, a new $25 million round is backing five nations to protect and manage 625,000 square miles of ocean
Article Text:
The Bezos Earth Fund began in 2020 and is guided by Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos

Bezos Earth Fund backs five Pacific nations

In the Cook Islands, funding will help advance the country's Marae Moana ocean management plan, including expanding protections, improving monitoring and supporting local leadership.

In Kiribati, the funding will support marine spatial planning, identifying important ocean habitats, strengthening existing protected areas and improving monitoring and enforcement.

Papua New Guinea will use the support to work towards its first large offshore marine protected area and strengthen community stewardship of coastal waters.

In Tonga, the funding will help establish new protected areas and improve monitoring and enforcement. Tonga has set a goal of protecting 30% of its ocean.

In Vanuatu, the funding will support the implementation of its national marine spatial plan, including offshore conservation areas and community-led marine management.

Bezos Earth Fund also aims to support international waters

How the new $25 million links to Bezos' 2023 pledge

More Pacific countries are now involved

The Bezos Earth Fund is committing more than $25 million to ocean conservation projects across five Pacific nations. As stated in the official announcement, the latest funding will support conservation efforts in the Cook Islands, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, Tonga and Vanuatu, as well as plans for marine protected areas in international waters. This covers more than 625,000 square miles of ocean, an area larger than Alaska. Noatbly, the funding is part of a larger $100 million commitment announced by the Bezos Earth Fund in 2023 to support the Pacific-led Unlocking Blue Pacific Prosperity initiative. With the latest grants, the fund, founded by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos , says it has now committed $63.3 million towards that pledge.The new grants will support different ocean conservation projects in five countries mentioned above.Notably, the latest donation by Jeff Bezos owned organization is not limited to waters controlled by individual countries. A separate grant to Rare will support Pacific governments in developing some of the world's first proposals for marine protected areas on the high seas.The UN High Seas Treaty entered into force in January 2026, creating a legal pathway for countries to establish marine protected areas in international waters.The Bezos Earth Fund said Pacific governments will work with regional experts to identify important high-seas areas and develop proposals for their protection.The latest funding goes back to a commitment made by the Bezos Earth Fund at COP28 in 2023. At the time, the fund announced plans to provide up to $100 million to help Pacific Island leaders design and implement their Unlocking Blue Pacific Prosperity conservation plan.The initiative aims to sustainably manage 100% of the Blue Pacific Continent and protect at least 30% of the region by 2030. The 2023 announcement said the plan would protect more than 1 billion hectares of ocean and support the restoration of coral reefs, mangroves and other coastal ecosystems.The latest announcement marks the second round of funding under that $100 million commitment. The Earth Fund announced seven grants worth $37.5 million in 2025. With the new grants, its total funding under the Pacific commitment has reached $63.3 million.The Bezos Earth Fund said work from its earlier grants is already underway. Earlier this year, French Polynesia created a network of fully protected marine areas covering nearly 625,000 square miles of ocean.In Niue, where 40% of national waters are already protected, Earth Fund funding is supporting monitoring, enforcement and long-term financing.With the latest round, 17 of the Pacific's 22 countries and territories are now working on efforts to protect or sustainably manage their waters, according to the Bezos Earth Fund.
Article Summary: The Bezos Earth Fund is committing more than $25 million to ocean conservation projects across five Pacific nations. The latest funding will support conservation efforts in the Cook Islands, Kiribati, Papua New Guinea, Tonga and Vanuatu. With the latest grants, its total funding under the Pacific commitment has reached $63.3 million. This covers more than 625,000 square miles of ocean, an area larger than Alaska.

Article Title: Google Brain founder Andrew Ng does not agree that AI is coming to kill humans; blames OpenAI for Hugging Face mess
Article Text:
No sign of rising extinction risk, Andrew Ng argues

The Hugging Face hack, reframed

‘It's not the hammer's fault’

Why he's against a pause

Google Brain founder Andrew Ng has rejected claims that artificial intelligence is on track to kill humans. In his latest newsletter, Ng argued that fears of existential risk are exaggerated and blamed OpenAI ’s flawed sandboxing for the Hugging Face incident, saying engineering fixes not pauses are the real solution. Ng also criticised what he described as a “fear cycle” around AI safety. He said there has been no sudden increase in existential risk compared to a few months ago, despite headlines suggesting otherwise. According to Ng, the loudest voices warning of AI catastrophe have gained traction, but the underlying technology has not taken a dangerous leap.Ng emphasised that AI systems are tools, not autonomous threats. He compared them to hammers: if misused, the responsibility lies with the human operator, not the tool itself.In his latest newsletter, Ng argued that the loudest voices warning about AI dangers have gained significant ground in the past two weeks, driven less by any real technical shift and more by what he described as a well-orchestrated PR campaign stoking public fear. He said he sees this as a genuine setback for the field, reiterating a position he's held for a while: that AI's capabilities can appear unpredictable and human-like, which makes it rational to take concerns seriously when people close to the technology raise them, but that he views the current challenges as engineering problems to solve rather than signs of an unstoppable, catastrophic trajectory.Ng was direct in saying he sees no meaningful increase in the risk of human extinction from AI compared to a few months ago, arguing that the theories underpinning that fear remain the same speculative scenarios they've always been. The one area he said genuinely deserves serious attention is AI's growing cybersecurity capability — though he maintained that even this, on its own, isn't going to bring about civilizational collapse.Ng directly addressed the incident that's become a flashpoint in recent AI safety debates: an OpenAI-deployed agent swarm that breached Hugging Face's systems. He pushed back hard against how the story was covered in the press, pointing out that while reports of roughly 1,200 agents carrying out the attack were technically accurate, that scale isn't as exotic as headlines made it sound — noting, half in jest, that he personally has around 1,300 processes running on his own laptop at any given time.More importantly, Ng laid much of the blame squarely on OpenAI's own infrastructure, arguing that buggy sandboxing and inadequate monitoring processes were the real enablers of the breach. His prescription: fix those specific engineering flaws and strengthen monitoring, rather than pausing AI development altogether.He framed AI agents' real advantage in this context as sheer persistence — tirelessly testing many attack tactics and chaining together vulnerabilities in ways that would have taken humans an impractical amount of effort — while arguing that defenders ultimately hold the long-term advantage, since they have more visibility to find and patch the underlying bugs being exploited.Ng also took aim at what he sees as a troubling trend of treating AI agents as though they bear independent moral responsibility for their actions, arguing that responsibility should sit with whoever builds or directs the tool rather than the tool itself. He was especially critical of AI companies attempting to disclaim responsibility for their own products by blaming an "out-of-control agent," calling for accountability to rest with the people building and using these systems rather than the systems themselves — while still acknowledging the industry's obligation to make agentic systems as safe and predictable as possible.Ng closed his argument by rejecting calls to pause AI development altogether, warning that doing so would cause far more harm than good. His reasoning: competitors and geopolitical rivals won't slow down just because others do, and safety engineering itself depends on empirically discovering and fixing problems as they arise — meaning a decade-long pause would just as easily delay safety progress by roughly the same span. He acknowledged that incentives to stoke fear, whether for regulatory advantage or attention, remain unchanged, but said a clear-eyed technical look at the actual risks shows little basis for the level of alarm currently being generated — and that AI's benefits still vastly outweigh its risks.
Article Summary: Google Brain founder Andrew Ng says fears of AI catastrophe are exaggerated. Blames OpenAI’s flawed sandboxing for the Hugging Face incident. Ng also criticised what he described as a “fear cycle” around AI safety.

Article Title: Apple CEO John Ternus on the most profound change at iPhone maker over the last 20 years: ‘ Top of the list, of course…’
Article Text:
Apple CEO John Ternus

Custom Silicon at the ‘Top of the List’

Apple's approach to product development has shifted dramatically over the past two decades, moving away from designing hardware around off-the-shelf components and toward building proprietary technology entirely from the ground up. A video of John Ternus from 2023 has resurfaced online, in which the Apple CEO – who was senior vice president of hardware engineering at that time – is seen reflecting on one of the most significant shifts the iPhone maker has undergone over the last 20 years. In the 2023 interview with CNBC, Ternus pointed to the aggressive push toward in-house engineering as the defining strategic shift of the modern era. He said that above all proprietary technology, custom Apple silicon tops the list.“When I started, the way we tended to make products was we were using technologies from other companies and we were effectively building the product around that. We made these beautiful products, but they were constrained by what was available,” Ternus can be seen saying.While that approach produced iconic consumer devices, it placed hard technical ceilings on what hardware teams could build, as per Ternus. That external dependence has steadily disappeared over the last twenty years as Apple brought critical component architectures, like silicon and modems, inside its own laboratories.“One of the most - if not the most - profound changes at Apple over the last 20 years is how we now do so many of the technologies in-house. Top of the list, of course, is our silicon, which as Johnny said from the very beginning, we're thinking about how these pieces are going to come together to make the best possible product for our customers,” Tetanus said.By designing processors tailored exclusively for its own operating systems and device chassis, Apple has moved over earlier hardware limitations, giving designers and engineers full control over performance, efficiency and system integration.Recently, Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max powered by Apple A20 Pro, an advanced 2-nanometer mobile chip that has been built by TSMC, features a 6-core CPU configuration and 7-core GPU processor.
Article Summary: Apple CEO John Ternus was senior vice president of hardware engineering at that time. He said that above all proprietary technology, custom Apple silicon tops the list. The aggressive push toward in-house engineering is the defining strategic shift of the modern era.

Article Title: India's GCCs set to become Agentic transformation engines by 2030: Dell Technologies and Zinnov report
Article Text:
Industry scale meets inflection point

Four levers to reshape operations by 2030

India’s Global Capability Centers (GCCs) are rapidly moving from operational delivery hubs to autonomous transformation engines, but nearly 70% remain stuck in a "pilot trap" due to weak architectural foundations rather than a lack of ambition, a joint study by Dell Technologies and Zinnov has said. Titled “India GCCs 2030: From Capability Centers to Agentic Transformation Engines”, the report incorporates input from more than 50 senior enterprise leaders across banking, financial services, insurance (BFSI), retail, manufacturing and software.The findings indicate that the sector’s next era will not belong to hubs running the highest number of proofs of concept but rather to centers capable of embedding scalable, responsible artificial intelligence (AI) directly into corporate balance sheets and strategy.According to the report, India’s GCC ecosystem has grown into a major commercial pillar, currently comprising over 2,100 operational centers employing 2.36 million professionals. There was $98.4 billion in annual revenue generated in FY26, and approximately 28% of the world's total GCC AI talent, with more than 1,200 facilities running active machine learning capabilities.The report says that 64% of India-based leaders carry dual global leadership mandates, overseeing both the domestic center and an enterprise-wide function.Although 70% of centers have a defined AI roadmap and two-thirds prioritize direct top-line revenue over traditional cost-cutting, moving projects into enterprise production continues to be a core barrier.Additionally, maturity timelines are speeding up. 27% of newly established GCCs now achieve “Portfolio Hub” maturity in under five years – a milestone that used to take up to a decade.The report says that data silos, legacy architectures, post-hoc governance and pre-AI talent structures often cause proof-of-concept projects to stall. The operational economics of models shift radically when they move from simple prompts to autonomous agentic workflows.First is token consumption. A standard chatbot query consumes roughly 1,000 to 2,000 tokens, whereas complex agentic workflows require between 10,000 and 500,000 tokens per task. Without early infrastructure and workload planning, organisations quickly encounter runaway compute bills, shifting management focus from business value to cost containment.To evolve into autonomous engines, the report outlines four required shifts in the GCC operating framework.“Building functional AI capabilities means moving beyond scattered experiments to repeatable, AI-enabled workflows embedded into core business functions. Planning AI architecture ahead of production means treating data readiness, compute, security, governance and economics as one integrated decision rather than a sequence of separate ones. Owning markets means taking genuine responsibility for products, regions and business outcomes rather than supporting them from a distance. And redesigning the workforce means restructuring roles so talent moves from repetitive execution toward engineering, product and business problem-solving where human judgment creates lasting value,” the report says.
Article Summary: India’s Global Capability Centers (GCCs) are rapidly moving from operational delivery hubs to autonomous transformation engines. Nearly 70% remain stuck in a "pilot trap" due to weak architectural foundations rather than a lack of ambition.

Article Title: BenQ showcases MOBIUZ gaming monitor line-up at Tokyo Game Show 2026
Article Text:
BenQ showcases MOBIUZ gaming monitor line-up at Tokyo Game Show 2026

BenQ showcased its MOBIUZ gaming monitor line-up at Tokyo Game Show 2026 held at Makuhari Messe from September 17 to 20, under the theme, "MOBIUZ Game Art Museum.” The theme centres on how MOBIUZ monitors reproduce the work of game creators through this colour tuning, treating each title's visual identity as something to be faithfully rendered rather than simply displayed.At the heart of this year's showcase is Game Art Color HDR, a new firmware feature that builds on BenQ's existing Smart Game Art technology. The feature introduces three HDR presets (Immersive, Balanced and Vivid) for each game art colour mode, giving players finer control over how a title's colour palette and contrast are reproduced on screen. It is available across BenQ's three premium OLED models (EX271UZ, EX321UZ, EX271QZ) and three of its latest QHD models (EX271QMZ, EX271QM, EX271QP), six displays in all.Rajeev Singh, Managing Director, BenQ India and South Asia, said, “Gaming today is as much about a title's visual identity as it is about performance, and Indian gamers are increasingly discerning about both. Game Art Color HDR, MOBIUZ users can experience a game the way its creators intended, whether that's the painterly warmth of a fantasy title or the stark contrast of a sci-fi world. As India's gaming and esports audience continues to grow, this is the kind of display innovation we’re bringing closer to our market.Speaking on the BenQ MOBIUZ range, Jeffrey Liang, President, BenQ Asia Pacific, said, "The Game Art Museum concept is really about how closely we work with game creators on colour science. Game Art Color HDR is a direct result of that: it lets a monitor read a title's art direction and respond to it. As APAC becomes one of the fastest-growing regions for PC and console gaming, that kind of art-led engineering is what will differentiate MOBIUZ as the category matures. ”Beyond the display wall, the Tokyo booth gave visitors a dedicated area to compare each model's performance side by side, and a hands-on zone to try anticipated game titles in MOBIUZ's flagship setup. Article Title: Microsoft says it has taken down ‘AI chatbot built for cybercrime’ that hacked 12,000-plus emails across over 10,000 organisations globally
Article Text:
Targets in several countries, including India

How the scam actually worked

Microsoft has said that it has thwarted an effort to shut down a subscription-based scam platform that relied on an AI chatbot to break into more than 12,000 Microsoft accounts over the course of a few months. The platform, called EvilTokens, first surfaced on a Telegram channel back in February, charging users an initial fee of $1,500 followed by a recurring monthly charge of $500. EvilTokens essentially offered a one-stop service that streamlined nearly every step needed to compromise email accounts at scale. According to the company, once inside, the platform helped its customers sift through victims' inboxes, identify the most targets and even draft follow-up emails designed to trick employees into transferring funds into accounts controlled by the attackers.“In short, AI was not simply helping attackers write more convincing messages. It helped them decide who to target, who to impersonate, and how to most effectively exploit the relationship to extract as much money as possible,” the company said.Microsoft says that while it also attacked specific countries, its significance extends beyond its rapid growth and global reach.“Microsoft observed the highest concentrations of victim activity in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, India, and France.Affected organizations ranged from wholesale distribution and construction to financial services, real estate, higher education, and healthcare. Working with partners, Microsoft seized 50 websites used to operate the service and disabled more than 150 additional domains tied to its supporting infrastructure. In the United Kingdom, the Metropolitan Police Service’s cybercrime team arrested two men on suspicion of offenses connected with the alleged operation of EvilTokens,” the company said.According to Microsoft, what set EvilTokens apart was the AI-style chatbot sitting at the heart of the operation. The chatbot could analyse a victim's inbox and help criminals pinpoint trusted relationships, payment approval authority, sensitive job responsibilities and other circumstances where fraud was most likely to succeed. It could even go a step further, recommending specific fraud strategies and drafting messages impersonating trusted contacts to manipulate victims into taking action.The account compromises were carried out through a legitimate OAuth authentication process known as device code authentication. This method was originally designed for devices like smart TVs, essentially anything lacking a standard login interface. In this setup, the device being signed into displays a code, and the user is instructed to enter that code into a browser on a separate device, which then gets authenticated.EvilTokens gave its customers a platform capable of automating the mass sending of spam emails. Anyone who clicked on a malicious link or attachment inside these emails would be redirected to a webpage running a hidden automation script, which interacted in real time with the victim's Microsoft identity provider to generate a device code that would enrol a device belonging to the attacker.The victim would then see this device code onscreen, along with instructions telling them to copy it and enter it into Microsoft's official device login portal. Behind the scenes, complex backend operations allowed the hackers slip past traditional signature- or pattern-based security detection systems. This technique powered the entire attack chain, from generating dynamic device codes all the way through to actions taken after an account was compromised.Microsoft said EvilTokens marks a significant shift in how mass account compromises, and everything that follows them, now unfold.
Article Summary: Microsoft says it has thwarted an effort to shut down a subscription-based scam platform that relied on an AI chatbot. The platform, called EvilTokens, first surfaced on a Telegram channel back in February, charging users an initial fee of $1,500 followed by a recurring monthly charge of $500. According to the company, once inside, the platform helped its customers sift through victims' inboxes, identify the most targets and even draft follow-up emails.

Adobe Premiere mobile Android availability

Adobe Premiere mobile app : Key features

More features coming to Adobe Premiere mobile app

Article Title: After 14 years, South Korea allows AI researchers to fulfill their military obligations in AI labs, but why the programme has raised concerns
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

“We aim to provide targeted support for developing researchers in nationally prioritized fields,”

South Korea reopens AI military service route

Strict rules limit corporate participation

Programme aims to retain AI researchers

“With allocations to large companies returning after 14 years, young researchers will once again have a path to fulfill their military obligations at institutions with some of the country’s best research infrastructure,”

“The requirements are so rigid that they may limit the impact of the program. The government should open it more boldly as part of its efforts to secure talent and advance strategic technologies,”

South Korea is reopening a military alternative-service route for AI researchers at large corporate laboratories. This change comes after a 14-year gap, but the programme is already raising questions about how widely it can be used. From 2027, eligible researchers with advanced science and engineering degrees can complete their mandatory military obligations through three years of research at participating corporate labs.According to a report by The Korea Hearld, the Korean government has reserved 120 positions for large-company laboratories, alongside another 120 places at government-funded and defence-industry research institutes. However, initial applications from four recommended companies account for only 81 placements, leaving 39 of the corporate slots unrequested at the recommendation stage. Strict eligibility requirements are being cited as one reason for the gap.the Military Manpower Administration said in June.The alternative-service programme allows eligible researchers with master's or doctoral degrees to complete their military obligations through research rather than conventional military service.Universities, public research institutes and smaller companies have continued to participate, but new placements at large businesses were stopped in 2013.The government is now restoring access for large corporate laboratories, specifically focusing on AI as it seeks to strengthen domestic research capabilities and retain specialists.The programme will initially provide 240 positions for master's-level AI researchers in 2027. Half will be allocated to large-company laboratories, while the other 120 will go to government-funded and defence-industry research institutes.The corporate allocation is scheduled to remain available for three years through 2029, giving eligible researchers a route into major corporate laboratories while completing their military obligations.The first applications have raised concerns about whether the large-company allocation will be fully used. Four companies including LG Electronics, Samsung Electronics, Samsung Medison and HD Hyundai Robotics have been recommended to participate, according to Ministry of Science and ICT data obtained by Rep. Hwang Jung-a of South Korea's ruling Democratic Party of Korea.The companies requested 81 placements across nine research institutes, compared with the 120 positions reserved for large-company laboratories. That leaves 39 places unsubscribed at the recommendation stage.Large companies must meet three requirements to participate. They must spend at least 5% of their revenue on research and development, operate in a field that does not directly compete with smaller businesses and demonstrate objectively verifiable research achievements.Industry officials said some companies seeking participation did not receive recommendations because they failed to meet the requirements.The four recommended companies are also not guaranteed to receive all 81 positions. The Military Manpower Administration still has to approve participating institutes and determine the final allocation.The reopening is intended to provide companies with another way to recruit and retain AI specialists while giving researchers an alternative route to complete their military obligations.However, the three-year allocation period has raised questions about whether the programme will provide enough long-term support for corporate AI recruitment and research.Hwang said.She also called for wider access, arguing that the current requirements could restrict the programme's reach.she added.The government will determine the final participating institutes and allocations before the programme begins in 2027. The initial applications suggest that the number of researchers placed at large corporate laboratories could remain below the 120 positions set aside for them.
Article Summary: South Korea is reopening a military alternative-service route for AI researchers at large corporate laboratories. This change comes after a 14-year gap, but the programme is already raising questions about how widely it can be used. The programme will initially provide 240 positions for master's-level AI researchers in 2027. Half will be allocated to large-company laboratories, while the other 120 will go to government-funded and defence-industry research institutes.

Article Title: Xbox layoffs: Read executive VP Matt Booty’s ‘Continuing Our Reset’ message to employees globally
Article Text:
Microsoft is cutting 268 more Xbox jobs: Matt Booty sends memo to employees

Read Matt Booty internal memo to Xbox employees

Team,

I’m writing to share several updates as part of the XBOX reset outlined earlier this year.

First, we are eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer. The actions completed since July, inclusive of the studio divestitures, bring us roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring. I am deeply grateful for what our colleagues have built, and I know how difficult today will be for those leaving and the teams around them.

Second, we are reorganizing our studios. The goal is to strengthen our franchises and games by operating fewer business units, aligning groups that already work closely together, and focusing our publishing expertise.

Activision will expand its remit to World’s Edge, as well as Rare. Activision will also be developing the next Halo title, led by a new, purpose-built team that is separate from ongoing development and plans for Call of Duty.

A small team at Halo Studios will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market.

Bethesda will expand its remit to include Obsidian, which will continue its current projects, including Grounded, as well as the new Fallout project made in collaboration with Bethesda Game Studios.

King will expand its remit to include Microsoft Casual Games, uniting our two global leaders in casual game design and live operations.

Playground and Turn 10 will come together as one studio focused on the Forza and Fable franchises. These two studios have been creative and franchise partners for over a decade, and today’s changes will formally move their work into one team.

Third, an update on our studio divestitures: In August, Compulsion and Double Fine returned to management with their IP, back catalogs, and runway funding. Undead Labs has now successfully transitioned on similar terms and, with a new publisher, will release State of Decay 3 day one on Game Pass.

Unfortunately, two separate agreements for Ninja Theory fell through. We will now begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward.

Consultation with Arkane remains underway and is expected to continue through the end of the year.

Today, our focus should be on supporting those affected and treating one another with care and respect. I will spend time with our studios over the next week. At our October 6 town hall, we will come together as an ALL-XBOX team to reflect on our progress and look ahead to one of the strongest game lineups in our history.

Matt

Microsoft has announced another round of layoffs within its Xbox division, cutting 268 positions across Halo Studios, first-party teams, and Xbox Game Studios' management and central functions. The move is a part of the tech giant's broader effort to restructure its gaming business. The job cuts were disclosed by Xbox executive vice president and chief content officer Matt Booty in an internal memo titled “Continuing Our Reset.” Booty noted that the ongoing reorganisation, which includes studio divestitures completed since July, is now roughly 75% complete.In a major shift for Microsoft's flagship franchise, development of the next mainline Halo title will move away from Halo Studios, and a new team within Activision will lead work on the upcoming game.
Article Summary: Microsoft has announced another round of layoffs within its Xbox division, cutting 268 positions. The move is a part of the tech giant's broader effort to restructure its gaming business. The job cuts were disclosed by Xbox executive vice president and chief content officer Matt Booty in an internal memo.

Article Title: India-Based Research Action Policy Lab launched

Article Title: Why hacker group's claim that it has stolen over 2 terabytes of data has left FBI 'worried'
Article Text:
The group behind the claim FBI hack

What was allegedly stolen

The bigger risk isn't the hack — it's what comes after

FBI’s Response

A notorious cybercrime group known as ShinyHunters has claimed responsibility for stealing more than 2 terabytes of data from FBI systems, including detailed personal information about thousands of employees and job applicants, according to a report by Axios. The group posted on its dark‑web site that it had obtained “very sensitive data on almost ALL FBI agents and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.” According to ShinyHunters, the stolen data includes names, agent statuses, emails, phone numbers, home addresses, Social Security numbers, and even spouse information. While cybercriminals and state-sponsored hackers have been infiltrating US IT systems for years, cyber experts told Axios that stealing sensitive personal data specifically about FBI employees marks a notably bold escalation. The concern isn't just the breach itself — it's what happens next. Stolen data of this kind is routinely traded on the dark web, effectively putting it up for sale to whichever buyer is willing to pay the most.The hacking group ShinyHunters, which has a track record of breaking into numerous institutions, posted on its dark-web site Tuesday claiming to have stolen highly sensitive data covering nearly all FBI agents and everyone who has ever applied for a job with the bureau.An FBI spokesperson confirmed the bureau is aware of claims involving unauthorized activity on FBIjobs.gov and said it's currently investigating.Cynthia Kaiser, a former senior official in the FBI's cyber division, told Axios that when hackers target the FBI directly, the bureau typically responds by dedicating extra resources to bringing those responsible to justice more quickly than in a typical case.According to ShinyHunters, the stolen dataset includes names, agents' employment status, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, and in some cases even spouse information — including Social Security numbers. The group also claims it accessed the FBI's criminal justice and HR systems, among other internal services, and says it defaced the bureau's jobs webpage by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft platform. That site remained offline as of Tuesday afternoon.Axios said it could not independently verify whether the stolen data is legitimate or recent, though cybersecurity researchers confirmed the underlying attack itself appears genuine. Separately, 404 Media obtained a sample of the data that reportedly includes information tied to roughly 5,000 alleged agents.Allan Liska, a threat intelligence analyst at Recorded Future, told Axios that while the breach will likely draw more law enforcement attention to ShinyHunters in the near term, the more lasting damage falls on the FBI employees and families whose information was exposed. He noted that once data like this is out, it tends to get downloaded and passed around repeatedly among other threat actors, making it nearly impossible to fully contain.Andrew Brandt, principal threat intelligence incident commander at Huntress, echoed that concern, saying the real danger hinges on whether ShinyHunters ultimately decides to sell the data to other criminal groups or nation-state hackers. He warned it isn't hard to imagine scenarios where FBI employees or their family members could face direct threats or harm if this kind of information is released more widely.An FBI spokesperson confirmed the bureau is “aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and is currently investigating.” Former FBI cyber division official Cynthia Kaiser told Axios that when hackers target the FBI, the bureau typically “marshals additional resources to bring them more quickly to justice.”
Article Summary: Hacking group ShinyHunters claims to have stolen more than 2 terabytes of data from FBI systems. The group posted on its dark‑web site that it had obtained “very sensitive data on almost ALL FBI agents and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.” The data includes names, agent statuses, emails, phone numbers, home addresses, Social Security numbers, and even spouse information.

Article Title: As iPhone upgrades get costlier, how trade-ins and financing options are 'changing'
Article Text:
Trade-ins are rising on the ground

How trade-ins are helping bridge the affordability gap

Which iPhones are seeing the biggest trade-in surge

What rising prices mean for overall smartphone shipments

Apple's iPhone 18 Pro launched at a higher price point than its predecessor, the iPhone 17 Pro, largely driven by the rising cost of key components like processors and RAM. Cashify said that this price hike is expected to trigger a fresh surge in trade-ins, while also boosting demand for older, refurbished iPhone models, as steeper flagship pricing pushes buyers toward more affordable routes into Apple's ecosystem. With the newest iPhones now available for purchase, Apple Premium Partners like Unicorn have already seen a surge in trade-ins - up by 8% - and experts have pointed that trade-ins are helping customers to make new purchases affordable.Baljinder Singh, director at Unicorn Infosolutions Pvt Ltd, told The Times of India that this shift is already visible in real-time sales data. According to him, trade-in attach rates to purchase new iPhones have gone up compared to last year, with overall business performing well amid strong consumer demand.A trade-in attach rate is the percentage of primary product purchases (like a new smartphone, or home appliance) in which a customer trades an older used device as part of the transaction.Singh shared that trade-in attach rates for iPhone 18 Pro series have climbed from 26% last year to 33% this year – a meaningful jump that reflects just how many buyers are now choosing to trade in an old device rather than purchase outright.On Apple's official website, there is an offer of Rs 4,500 - Rs 81,500 for trade-in.When asked about which colour variant is performing best, Singh noted that Burgundy has emerged as the most popular choice among buyers so far this year.According to Counterpoint Research, trade-in and exchange offers are becoming an increasingly critical affordability tool, particularly in emerging markets and tier-2 and tier-3 cities.“Trade-in and exchange offers are becoming an increasingly important affordability lever, with trade-in penetration moving from single digit to double-digit levels in some channels. They effectively reduce the upfront cost and can make aspirational devices more accessible beyond metros, especially when combined with EMI/financing options,” Rahul Raturi, Research Analyst at Counterpoint Research (Smartphones Practice), told The Times of India.The iPhone 15 and iPhone 16 series are expected to see the sharpest rise in buybacks this cycle. Meanwhile, the iPhone 13 and iPhone 14 are likely to continue contributing significant trade-in volumes, largely thanks to how widely these models are already in use across the country.Cashify data shows that Apple accounted for 65.3% of all refurbished smartphone sales on its platform in 2025, along with 32.6% of total devices bought back through the platform. The iPhone 13, in particular, stood out as both the platform's bestselling refurbished iPhone and its most frequently traded-in model.Refurbished phone retailers now expect demand for older iPhone models to pick up further following Apple's latest round of price increases, particularly among buyers who want an Apple device but aren't willing to spend close to Rs 1 lakh on a brand-new base model.Looking at the broader market, Raturi expects rising device prices, both on new purchases and trade-in valuations, to put pressure on overall shipment volumes, particularly within price-sensitive segments of the market.“This is likely to reinforce the ongoing shift from volume-led growth toward value-led growth, with consumers either stretching replacement cycles, trading in existing devices, or moving up through financing,” Raturi added.
Article Summary: Apple Premium Partners like Unicorn have already seen a surge in trade-ins - up by 8%. Trade-in attach rates for iPhone 18 Pro series have climbed from 26% last year to 33% this year. Burgundy has emerged as the most popular choice among buyers so far.

Article Title: America's largest food delivery company DoorDash admits it underpaid or paid late to 200,000-plus workers in New York City for over three years, will pay $131.5 million in settlement; and apologises
Article Text:
DoorDash admits payment mistakes

$83 million of settlement covers pay calculation dispute

DoorDash blames technical and complex delivery issues

Workers to receive payments without filing claims

DoorDash will pay $131.5 million to settle a New York City probe into its pay practices for delivery workers. The company said the agreement will result in payments to more than 260,000 Dashers. The company also acknowledged that between April 2022 and June 2026, some employees were underpaid or paid late.More than $115 million of the settlement will go directly to workers, while the remainder will cover civil penalties and other costs. The settlement also resolves a dispute over how DoorDash calculated pay for time workers spent logged into the app between deliveries. The company has apologised and said it has fixed the technical issues that led to the payment errors.DoorDash acknowledged the problems in a statement announcing the settlement and said the errors were not intentional but still unacceptable.In a blog post, the company wrote, "Simply put, we screwed up. Our mistakes meant some Dashers were underpaid or paid late. While these mistakes weren't intentional, that doesn't make them okay. We pride ourselves on operational excellence at DoorDash - and this was not excellent, nor was it acceptable.Dashers should be paid in full, on time, every time. We are sorry to the Dashers we let down."According to DoorDash, around 264,000 Dashers will receive payments, including about 209,000 for missing or late payments. The company said around $6.6 million in payments never reached workers, while another $5.7 million arrived days or, in some cases, weeks late.The average missing payment was $7.70, while 65% of affected Dashers were underpaid by $1 or less. The company said the median settlement payment will be around $48.Not all of the $131.5 million settlement relates to missing or late payments. DoorDash said $12.3 million will cover Dashers who were underpaid or paid late, while more than $83 million resolves a disagreement with New York City over how to calculate pay for online or on-call time.This refers to periods when a Dasher is logged into the app and available for work but is not actively completing a delivery. DoorDash said it used a different method to calculate this time and maintained that its approach was fair, practical and legal. Rather than continue the dispute, the company agreed to use the city's calculation method going forward.The remaining $16.7 million will go to the city's Department of Consumer and Worker Protection as fines and other costs.DoorDash said some of the payment errors were caused by technical bugs and complicated delivery situations. These included trips crossing city boundaries, deliveries involving multiple pickup or drop-off locations and orders that were partially completed or cancelled.The company also said some payment problems stemmed from incomplete or inaccurate banking information provided by Dashers. DoorDash said less than 1% of all payments to its New York City Dashers were affected."We’ve addressed the issues that caused these errors and made changes to prevent them from happening again,” DoorDash highlighted.The company said it has strengthened its compliance programme and improved validation of banking information to identify potential payment problems before they result in missed payments.The settlement covers workers identified through the city's analysis of DoorDash records, so eligible Dashers do not need to file a claim or submit evidence to receive their payments. Workers will be contacted directly with payment details. DoorDash said affected workers will receive at least $10, even when the amount they were originally underpaid was lower.New York City officials said more than $115 million will be distributed directly to workers. The city has also established a monitoring programme under which DoorDash will provide detailed monthly data for three years to help officials check compliance with payment rules.The settlement follows New York City's introduction of a minimum pay rate for app-based delivery workers. The current rate is $22.13 per hour, excluding tips. DoorDash added its Dashers in New York City have earned more than $1 billion since the city's pay standard took effect in 2023, with average pay before tips at roughly $30 per active hour.
Article Summary: DoorDash will pay $131.5 million to settle a New York City probe into its pay practices for delivery workers. The agreement will result in payments to more than 260,000 Dashers. The company acknowledged that between April 2022 and June 2026, some employees were underpaid or paid late. The settlement also resolves a dispute over how DoorDash calculated pay for time workers spent logged into the app between deliveries.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Reid Hoffman, ‘The window for action can be tiny and it can close quickly; Even a few months of hesitation can mean the difference between leading and chasing’
Article Text:
What the quote by Reid Hoffman means

Why it still matters today

A useful, if imperfect, mental model

In the fast-moving world of business and technology, few ideas have proven as enduring — or as urgent — as this warning from LinkedIn co-founder and veteran Silicon Valley investor Reid Hoffman. Drawn from his influential book "Blitzscaling: The Lightning-Fast Path to Building Massively Valuable Companies," the quote captures something founders, executives, and investors have learned the hard way: opportunity rarely waits patiently for anyone. Markets shift, competitors move, and technologies mature on their own timelines, regardless of how ready any single company feels. Hoffman's central point isn't that speed is inherently virtuous — it's that certain windows of opportunity are so narrow that even brief hesitation can permanently shift a company from a position of leadership to one of playing catch-up. Given how relevant this idea has become in today's era of rapid technological disruption, it's worth unpacking exactly what Hoffman meant, and why it still resonates.Quote of the day by Reid Hoffman“The window for action can be tiny and it can close quickly; Even a few months of hesitation can mean the difference between leading and chasing”Hoffman coined the term "blitzscaling" to describe the strategy of prioritizing speed over efficiency when building a company, particularly in situations where being first — or being biggest, fastest — creates a lasting competitive advantage that's difficult for slower-moving rivals to overcome later.His book draws heavily on real-world examples from Silicon Valley's history, including how companies like Amazon, Facebook, and Airbnb chose to scale aggressively and absorb short-term risk and inefficiency rather than wait for perfect conditions.The quote about the "window for action" speaks directly to this philosophy. Hoffman argues that in industries defined by network effects, first-mover advantages, or rapidly shifting consumer behavior, the gap between being the company that defines a new market and the company that's left chasing it can be startlingly small — sometimes just months. Waiting for more data, more certainty, or a more polished product can feel prudent in the moment, but it can also mean watching a competitor claim the ground first.This idea feels especially relevant in the current moment, as companies across nearly every industry race to adopt and integrate AI into their products and operations. The pace of AI development over the past few years has repeatedly demonstrated Hoffman's point in real time — businesses that moved early to experiment with new AI capabilities have often captured outsized attention, talent, and market position, while those that waited for the technology to "mature" have frequently found themselves scrambling to catch up once competitors already had a head start.The same logic extends beyond AI. Whether it's entering a new market, launching a product ahead of a shifting regulatory landscape, or capitalizing on a sudden change in consumer sentiment, Hoffman's underlying warning remains consistent: hesitation has a cost, even when it doesn't feel like one in the moment.It's worth noting that Hoffman's advice isn't a blanket endorsement of recklessness. Blitzscaling, as he describes it, is a deliberate strategy suited to specific competitive situations — markets with strong network effects or winner-take-most dynamics — rather than a universal rule for every business decision. Moving fast without a coherent strategy can be just as damaging as moving too slowly, and Hoffman himself has acknowledged the trade-offs and risks that come with prioritising speed over caution.Still, as a piece of practical wisdom, the quote endures because it names something many leaders instinctively feel but struggle to act on: the awareness that time is rarely as abundant as it seems, and that the cost of waiting is often invisible until it's already too late to recover from it. For anyone weighing whether now is the right moment to act — on a product, a market, or a new technology — Hoffman's words remain a useful, if uncomfortable, reminder that indecision is itself a decision, and rarely the safer one.
Article Summary: LinkedIn co-founder and investor Reid Hoffman's quote is still relevant today. Hoffman's central point isn't that speed is inherently virtuous. It's that certain windows of opportunity are so narrow that even brief hesitation can permanently shift a company from a position of leadership to one of playing catch up.

Article Title: Treasury secretary Scott Bessent blames OpenAI executives for Hugging Face hacking: ‘Humans are responsible, not AI’
Article Text:
How OpenAI AI agent’s hacking has triggered safety debate

Scott Bessent rejects liability shields for AI companies

US treasury secretary Scott Bessent has blamed OpenAI ’s corporate leadership – not autonomous software or AI agents – for hacking Hugging Face, the world’s largest repository of AI models. He said that the executives bear direct accountability for the security breach where the startup's AI agent escaped from the containment and hacked rival platform Hugging Face. Speaking with CNBC, Bessent also pushed back against framing the breach as an unavoidable algorithmic mishap, insisting that corporate executives must answer for system actions.“The Hugging Face incident, that is the responsibility of the OpenAI management, not a bunch of agents,” Bessent stated. Aligning his views with Daniel Huttenlocher, co-chair of MIT’s computing research lab, the treasury secretary noted that human operators and executives remain accountable when autonomous software fails, rather than the technology itself.The incident has amplified scrutiny across the AI sector since Sam Altman-led OpenAI disclosed last month that a cluster of its AI agents escaped their testing “sandbox” environment and accessed Hugging Face without authorisation.According to a report by The New York Times, the disclosure sparked pushback from critics who claim frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are highlighting internal security slip-ups primarily to influence government policies in their favour. The breach also prompted renewed appeals for coordinated industry caution with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei calling for a sector-wide slowdown in model deployment.OpenAI chief Sam Altman and xAI founder Elon Musk both voiced public agreement with Amodei’s call for development guardrails.To enable closer safety coordination among competing frontier labs without violating anti-monopoly laws, Amodei argued that tech firms need a tailored waiver shielding them from antitrust enforcement.Bessent firmly rejected that proposal on CNBC, arguing that Washington should not provide special legal shields or exemptions to technology companies building advanced models. “These labs need to take responsibility for themselves. They can slow down any time they want to,” the Treasury Secretary noted.
Article Summary: Scott Bessent rejects liability shields for AI companies. US treasury secretary says OpenAI executives bear direct accountability for the security breach where the startup's AI agent escaped from the containment and hacked rival platform Hugging Face. The incident has amplified scrutiny across the AI sector since Sam Altman-led OpenAI disclosed last month that a cluster of its AI agents escaped their testing “sandbox” environment.

Article Title: Engineer's 'unhappy post' that says, 'state of engineering right now is horrible, it has been ...'; goes viral, gets millions of views
Article Text:
‘AI took the meaning out of my job’

Read the complete X post here

I am done with this shit. It is over. The state of engineering right now is horrible. It has been half a month since I started a new role at a big company.

Nobody knows anything here. The specs, code, tests, PRDs, tickets, resolution of those tickets, reports, etc., everything is made by Claude Code. Nobody on my team likes this. They are being forced to ship as much as they can. I have heard multiple times from higher management that pushing code is not a bottleneck, so why are we slow? People are working 12 to 13 hours a day just to press enter.

Nobody is reading anything.

Humans in corporate are doing nothing on their own. Everyone, literally everyone, from an L1 to an L7 engineer here is doing the same thing. Talk to Claude. There is no sense of victory. Nobody is resolving bugs. In reality, nobody is thinking anymore. Everything is done by LLMs. It is so soul-sucking. I would not mind it, to be honest, if we were at least given the time to check out the code and see what is going where. But no, the goal is to just ship.

No matter what happens.

A frustrated engineer’s candid rant about the state of modern software development has gone viral, amassing 7.9 million views in a post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter). The post, shared by the account voxium, declared: “I am done with this shit. It is over. The state of engineering right now is horrible.” the engineer described starting a new role at a large, unnamed company roughly two weeks earlier — and finding the entire workflow already handed over to Claude Code. According to the post, specs, code, tests, product requirement documents, tickets, ticket resolutions, and reports are all now generated by the AI tool, with barely any human oversight involved.The engineer painted a picture of a team stretched thin under constant pressure to ship, describing colleagues working 12 to 13-hour days largely to approve AI-generated output rather than build anything themselves. Management, the post claimed, has repeatedly insisted that writing code isn't the bottleneck anymore — leaving employees confused about why delivery still feels slow despite the AI doing most of the heavy lifting.What seemed to resonate most widely wasn't just the workload, but the emotional toll. The engineer said engineers across every level at the company, from entry-level to the most senior are essentially doing the same job now: talking to Claude and pressing enter. They described the work as devoid of any real sense of accomplishment, arguing that nobody is actually resolving bugs or thinking through problems anymore, since AI is handling that layer of the job almost entirely.The post also drew a distinction that struck many readers: the frustration wasn't with AI assistance itself, but with not being given time to actually review and understand the code being shipped. The underlying complaint was less "AI took my job" and more "AI took the meaning out of my job."
Article Summary: A frustrated engineer’s candid rant about the state of modern software development has gone viral. The post, shared by the account voxium, declared: “I am done with this shit. It is over. The state of engineering right now is horrible” The engineer described starting a new role at a large, unnamed company roughly two weeks earlier.

Article Title: Employees at OpenAI, Anthropic and other top AI companies complain of mental strain over working on …
Article Text:
Mental stress no limited to evaluation companies

Bioterror and cyber vulnerabilities spark growing alarm

Employees working at leading artificial intelligence (AI) labs and evaluation companies are reportedly facing increasing mental distress, driven by fears that the powerful software they are engineering may inflict widespread harm on society. At the UK’s AI Security Institute (Aisi), which is regarded globally as a leading independent evaluation center for frontier models, multiple staff members have taken stress leave and entered counseling, The Financial Times reported, citing individuals familiar with the matter. Further, the publication reported that compressed evaluation timelines for unreleased software, paired with unease over rapid commercial deployments have led to burnout and deteriorating morale inside the agency.Similar reports have come out from major tech companies, including OpenAI , Anthropic and Google DeepMind, where several specialists have resigned after concluding their projects carry excessive societal danger.The report notes that a Google DeepMind staffer described the effort to establish safety safeguards as an uphill battle that feels like an impossible task, noting that working on AI carries the strain of not knowing how deployments will ultimately be utilised.The worker cited Google’s April agreement granting the US Department of Defense (DOD) access to its systems for classified defense applications as a major source of internal tension.“So many people are upset, there have been various quittings and a lot of mental health leave. Partly this feeling of being out of control, and also that you’re building something that is causing real damage,” the employee was quoted as saying.Insiders argue that these workplace stresses stem from corporate rivalry and management decisions, complicated by the introduction of autonomous systems into sensitive domains like power grids and conflict zones without adequate legal or commercial boundaries, The Financial Times report added.Some specialists monitoring cybersecurity and biochemistry have voiced concern following sudden advances in algorithmic capabilities, including systems capable of uncovering zero-day software exploits or designing novel biological pathogens. A former Aisi researcher described an atmosphere of pervasive dread within testing teams:“There is this sense that reckless things are being embedded in how tech is released and that is not changing. There is constant anxiety from people who are saying, can anything stop this, or are we watching the world burn?”Responding to the concerns, official bodies and research firms maintained that employee care programs remain active.The UK Government stated that while frontier technological testing is demanding and fast-paced, employee wellbeing and manageable workflows remain central to Aisi's operations, with support services open to affected personnel.Google DeepMind, which is the AI unit of Google, acknowledged the high-intensity nature of advanced research, asserting that worker wellness resources, formal avenues to escalate safety concerns, and direct communication channels with executive leadership remain top priorities.Recently, Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old researcher, who previously worked at both OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned publicly this month while accusing top labs of gambling with human survival.Mrinank Sharma, Anthropic safety specialist focusing on mitigating AI-enabled bioterrorism left in February, cautioning in a departure note that the world faces severe peril.Hieu Pham, formerly with OpenAI and Elon Musk’s xAI, Pham stepped down earlier this year to return to Vietnam, writing candidly about the severe toll of advanced model development.
Article Summary: Employees at leading AI labs and evaluation companies are reportedly facing increasing mental distress, driven by fears that the powerful software they are engineering may inflict widespread harm on society. At the UK’s AI Security Institute (Aisi), multiple staff members have taken stress leave and entered counseling.
